2027-06-14.title: Monday of the fourth week after Pentecost · Elisha the Prophet
readings: Present your members to God as instruments of righteousness
None of them was cleansed except Naaman the Syrian
2027-06-14.alt: Season of Pentecost, the week after the Fourth Sunday after Pentecost. The Panchangam remembers Elisha the Prophet (Eliša Nbiya). The Apostles' Fast (Shleeha Nombu) begins on Wednesday 16 June.
2027-06-14.verse: There were also many lepers in Israel in the time of the prophet Elisha, and none of them was cleansed except Naaman the Syrian.
theo: Today the Panchangam remembers Elisha the Prophet, and the Gospel names him. Elisha was a farmer's son, ploughing with twelve yoke of oxen, when Elijah passed by and threw his mantle over him; he left the plough, killed the oxen, fed the people with the meat and followed (1 Kings 19:19–21). When Elijah was about to be taken up, Elisha asked for one thing: “Please let me inherit a double share of your spirit.” The Books of Kings then tell of a ministry full of mercy: water made sweet, a poor widow's oil that flowed until every borrowed jar was full, a dead child given back to his mother at Shunem, a hundred people fed with twenty loaves of barley and some left over. Even after his death, a dead man who touched his bones came to life. The Fathers saw in Elisha a figure of Christ, who also fed the crowds, raised the dead and gave his Spirit in full measure to his disciples. Many Eastern Churches keep his memory on this day, and so do we, two days before the Apostles' Fast begins.

In the Gospel Jesus has just read from Isaiah in the synagogue of Nazareth and announced that the Scripture is fulfilled. His neighbours admire him, and then begin to doubt: is this not Joseph's son? Jesus answers with two stories from their own Scriptures: “But the truth is, there were many widows in Israel in the time of Elijah, when the heaven was shut up three years and six months, and there was a severe famine over all the land; yet Elijah was sent to none of them except to a widow at Zarephath in Sidon. There were also many lepers in Israel in the time of the prophet Elisha, and none of them was cleansed except Naaman the Syrian.” A Gentile widow and a Syrian army commander: God's mercy had always reached beyond the borders people drew around it. Origen, preaching on this passage, saw in Naaman a figure of the nations who would be cleansed through the true Elisha, our Lord, in the waters of Baptism (Homilies on Luke 33, in substance). Jesus is not insulting his own people; he is reminding them, as a prophet of Israel, of what Israel's own prophets had already shown. But the truth stings: “When they heard this, all in the synagogue were filled with rage.” They try to throw him from the cliff. “But he passed through the midst of them and went on his way.” No anger can stop the mission of mercy. It will go on, through Galilee to Jerusalem, and through the apostles to the ends of the earth, and to Kerala.

St Paul tells us today how that mercy takes hold of a life: “Therefore, do not let sin exercise dominion in your mortal bodies, to make you obey their passions. No longer present your members to sin as instruments of wickedness, but present yourselves to God as those who have been brought from death to life, and present your members to God as instruments of righteousness. For sin will have no dominion over you, since you are not under law but under grace.” Naaman went down into the Jordan proud and came up clean; we went down into the waters of Baptism and came up from death to life. St Ambrose taught the newly baptised that Naaman was healed not by the water of the Jordan alone but by the word of God and grace working in it, and that the same is true of the font (On the Mysteries 3–4, in substance). But the old habits of the body and the tongue still pull at us; the Catechism calls this the struggle left to us after Baptism, a struggle in which grace gives us the victory (Catechism 1264). On Wednesday the Apostles' Fast begins. It is a time to take back our members from sin and to offer them to God: eyes that look with purity, a tongue that blesses, hands that give, a stomach that learns to say no, feet that go to those in need. Like Elisha, let us ask for a double share of the Spirit, and like Naaman, let us humbly go down into the water of repentance.
outline: Ask: which part of me, eyes, tongue, hands or appetite, still serves sin rather than God?
From the plough to the prophet's mantle; a double share of the Spirit and a ministry of mercy.
God's mercy beyond borders, the anger at Nazareth, and Jesus who passes through the midst of them.
Baptised from death to life, we offer our members to God: preparing for the Apostles' Fast.
“Present your members to God as instruments of righteousness.”
live: Before Wednesday, decide on one concrete way to offer your body to God during the Apostles' Fast: a meal, a habit of the eyes or the tongue, an hour of the phone given to prayer.
Do one act of kindness this week for someone outside your usual circle of family, caste, community or language.
2027-06-14.prayer: Lord Jesus Christ, you are the prophet greater than Elijah and Elisha; your mercy reached the widow of Zarephath and Naaman the Syrian, and it has reached us. In Baptism you brought us from death to life: do not let sin rule in our mortal bodies, but make our members instruments of righteousness. As the Apostles' Fast draws near, give us, as you gave Elisha, a double share of your Spirit, and the humility of Naaman to go down into the waters of repentance. When anger or prejudice rises against your word, pass through the midst of it and carry your mercy on its way. You live and reign with the Father and the Holy Spirit, for ever. Amen.
altar: Elisha fed a hundred with twenty loaves and some were left; at the altar the true Prophet feeds the multitude with his own Body and Blood, and those brought from death to life in Baptism are made his members, instruments of righteousness.
conn: Luke 4:27 recalls 2 Kings 5:1–14, where Naaman the Syrian is healed after washing seven times in the Jordan at Elisha's word; Luke 4:25–26 recalls Elijah and the widow of Zarephath (1 Kings 17:8–16).

2 Kings 4:42–44 (a hundred fed with twenty loaves, with some left over) and 2 Kings 4:32–37 (a dead son given back to his mother) are echoed in the feeding of the crowds and the raising of the widow's son at Nain (Luke 7:11–17).
Romans 6:3–4 speaks of being buried with Christ in Baptism; today's verses 12–14 draw the moral consequence, which the Apostles' Fast (16–29 June) puts into practice.
fathers: Naaman the Syrian, cleansed when the lepers of Israel were not, is a figure of the nations cleansed by the spiritual Elisha, our Lord and Saviour, in the mystery of Baptism (Homilies on Luke 33, in substance).

Naaman doubted when told to wash in the Jordan, yet he was healed; so the newly baptised should believe that it is not the water alone that cleanses, but the grace and power of God working through it (On the Mysteries 3–4, in substance).
magis: After Baptism certain consequences of sin remain, among them the inclination to sin that Tradition calls concupiscence; it is left for us to wrestle with, and it cannot harm those who do not consent but resist it manfully by the grace of Jesus Christ (in substance).
Interior penance can be expressed in many ways, and Scripture and the Fathers insist above all on three forms: fasting, prayer and almsgiving.
The way of perfection passes by way of the Cross; there is no holiness without renunciation and spiritual battle.

quick: The Panchangam remembers Elisha the Prophet, disciple of Elijah, who asked for a double share of his spirit and worked many signs of mercy.
At Nazareth Jesus recalls that Elisha cleansed Naaman the Syrian: God's mercy reaches beyond every border; the angry crowd cannot stop him.
Paul urges the baptised not to let sin rule their bodies but to present their members to God as instruments of righteousness: a programme for the Apostles' Fast, which begins on Wednesday.
2027-06-14.action: Decide today what you will offer to God during the Apostles' Fast.
2027-06-14.question: Which of my members, eyes, tongue, hands or appetite, most needs to be given back to God?

family.explain: Long ago there was a prophet called Elisha. A soldier from another country, Naaman, had a terrible skin disease. A little servant girl from Israel told his wife about Elisha. Naaman went to the prophet, washed seven times in the river Jordan, and was healed. Jesus told this story to show that God loves people of every nation. On Wednesday our Church begins the Apostles' Fast, when we try to give our eyes, our mouths and our hands to God.
family.intention: We pray for people of every country and every religion, that they may know God's love; and we pray for a good beginning to the Apostles' Fast.
family.ask: Ask: “What will each of us give to God during the Apostles' Fast?”

illus: A young man from a parish in Pathanamthitta district went to work in a city in the north of India. In his hostel there was a boy from another state and another religion who was very ill with jaundice, and nobody went near him because he could not speak their language. The young man had been planning to keep the Apostles' Fast by giving up meat. Instead, he spent the fast going to the boy's room every evening with rice gruel and water, sitting with him and taking him to the hospital twice. When the boy recovered, he asked why a stranger had looked after him. The young man did not know how to explain, so he said: in my Church we are fasting now, and this was my fast. Later he told his parish priest that he had learned more about the Gospel in those two weeks than in years of catechism.

pm.open: Lord Jesus, give us a double share of your Spirit, and make our members instruments of righteousness as we prepare for the Apostles' Fast. Amen.
share: Present your members to God as instruments of righteousness (Romans 6:13). Which part of my life do I most need to give back to God?
None of them was cleansed except Naaman the Syrian (Luke 4:27). Whom do I find it hard to believe God loves?
But he passed through the midst of them and went on his way (Luke 4:30). Where do I need Jesus to pass through anger or opposition in my life?
pm.resp: Lord, make us instruments of your righteousness.
interc: For the Church, that her mercy may reach beyond every border, as the mercy of Elisha reached Naaman.
For all the baptised, that sin may not rule in their bodies, and that they may live as people brought from death to life.
For those suffering from skin diseases, leprosy and every illness that isolates people, and for those who care for them.
For migrants and strangers in our towns, that they may find neighbours who care for them.
For our parish, that the Apostles' Fast beginning on Wednesday may be kept with prayer, fasting and generosity.
pm.close: Father, through your prophets you showed mercy to the stranger, and in your Son you have brought us from death to life. Give us a double share of your Spirit, make our bodies instruments of righteousness, and let the Apostles' Fast renew us in grace. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

term: The Syriac word for prophet (from the same root as the Hebrew nabi), used in the Panchangam's “Eliša Nbiya” for Elisha the Prophet. In the West Syriac tradition the prophets of the Old Testament are remembered in the liturgy as those who foretold Christ and prepared his way.
kidsaint: Elisha and the little servant girl

Naaman was a great army commander, but he had a terrible skin disease. In his house there was a little girl from Israel who had been taken away from her home. She could have been angry and sad, but instead she said: I wish my master would go to the prophet Elisha; he would heal him! Naaman went, washed seven times in the river Jordan as Elisha told him, and was healed. Lesson: even a child can help someone find God's love.

homily: Dear friends, today the Panchangam remembers Elisha the Prophet. He was ploughing his field when Elijah threw his mantle over him, and he left everything to follow. Before Elijah was taken up, Elisha asked: Please let me inherit a double share of your spirit (2 Kings 2:9). God gave it, and Elisha's life was full of mercy: oil for a poor widow, a child raised to life, bread for the hungry, healing for a foreign soldier.

In the Gospel Jesus reminds the people of Nazareth: there were also many lepers in Israel in the time of the prophet Elisha, and none of them was cleansed except Naaman the Syrian (Luke 4:27). God's mercy reached beyond the borders people expected. The people were filled with rage, but he passed through the midst of them and went on his way (Luke 4:30). Nothing can stop the mercy of God.

St Paul shows us what that mercy does in us: present yourselves to God as those who have been brought from death to life, and present your members to God as instruments of righteousness (Romans 6:13). Like Naaman in the Jordan, we went down into the water of Baptism and came up clean. Now our eyes, our tongues, our hands and our feet belong to God.

On Wednesday the Apostles' Fast begins. Let us decide now what we will offer: a meal, a habit, our time, our care for a stranger. Let us ask, like Elisha, for a double share of the Spirit, and let us offer our bodies to God as instruments of his righteousness. Amen.
kids: Children, today we remember Elisha, a prophet who helped many people with God's power. A soldier called Naaman was very sick, and a little girl in his house told his wife about Elisha. Naaman went to the river Jordan, washed seven times, and was healed! Jesus said God loves people from every country. On Wednesday our Church begins the Apostles' Fast. You can give something to God too: maybe kind words, sharing your snacks, or saying your prayers without being told.

intro: Theme: “Present your members to God as instruments of righteousness.”
On Monday of the fourth week after Pentecost, the memory of Elisha the Prophet, two days before the Apostles' Fast: a double share of the Spirit, mercy beyond borders, and bodies offered to God.

points.h: Elisha: a double share of the Spirit
sub: From the plough to the mantle.
A ministry of mercy: oil, bread, life.
q: Please let me inherit a double share of your spirit.
The prayer of the righteous is powerful and effective.
points.apply: Ask the Holy Spirit each morning of the Apostles' Fast for the grace you most need.

points.h: Naaman the Syrian: mercy beyond borders
sub: A widow of Sidon and a Syrian soldier.
He passed through the midst of them.
q: his flesh was restored like the flesh of a young boy, and he was clean.
I truly understand that God shows no partiality, but in every nation anyone who fears him and does what is right is acceptable to him.
points.apply: Do one kindness this week for someone of another community, language or religion.

sub: Brought from death to life in Baptism.
Sin will have no dominion: grace, not law.
The Apostles' Fast: giving back our members to God.
q: Let the words of my mouth and the meditation of my heart be acceptable to you, O Lord, my rock and my redeemer.
present your bodies as a living sacrifice, holy and acceptable to God, which is your spiritual worship.
points.apply: Write down the one offering you will make during the Apostles' Fast and place it before the image of Christ at home.

concl: Elisha's spirit, Naaman's cleansing and Paul's call all point to Christ, whose mercy reaches every nation and whose grace releases us from the rule of sin.
The Apostles' Fast is the time to offer our members to God as instruments of righteousness.
2027-06-14.resolve: Ask for a double share of the Spirit, cross one border in kindness, and choose your offering for the Apostles' Fast.
